name: Turbo Energy, S.A.

profile.description: Turbo Energy, S.A. is a Valencia, Spain-based maker of solar energy storage systems. Its main products are the SUNBOX all-in-one inverter-and-battery units for homes and businesses and SUNBOX Industry systems (30 kW-2,000 kW). Both are managed by a cloud platform that uses AI to optimize charging and discharging against consumption, power prices, and weather. The company is majority-owned by Umbrella Solar Investment, listed on Nasdaq in September 2023, and is led by CEO Mariano Soria and Chairman Enrique Selva. H1 2026 revenue rose about 173% to €15.0M, driven by a 366 MWh industrial storage project.

innovation.label: DEVELOPING
innovation.analysis: Track Record (2/3): SUNBOX Industry, launched in 2024, opened a utility and industrial storage business. Its 366 MWh project drove H1 2026 revenue up about 173% to €15.0M [1][2]. AI Deployment (2/2): AI-driven energy management ships in every SUNBOX. The cloud platform analyzes consumption, market prices, and weather forecasts to schedule battery use for peak shaving and lower bills [3][4]. Market Share (0/2): Turbo is a sub-$25M-revenue niche player competing against Chinese inverter and battery giants and has no measurable share leadership [2]. Pipeline (1/2): The company has named products (SUNBOX Home Lite) and a U.S. market entry, but discloses no quantified order pipeline or launch revenue targets [4]. R&D Intensity (0/1): We found no disclosed R&D spending above industry norms. Total operating expenses fell 20.7% in H1 2026 [1].

inspiration.label: WEAK
inspiration.analysis: Mission Floor (1/4): Turbo frames its purpose as making intelligent solar storage accessible to homes and businesses. This is generic for the clean-energy hardware category and is not tied to any distinctive commitment [3][4]. Community Impact (0/2): We found no foundation, charitable program, or quantified community investment. Employee Retention (0/2): We found no retention or tenure data. The founder-CEO moved to the chairman role in late 2023 because of governance needs at the parent company [3]. Insider Buying (0/2): We found no insider open-market buying. Instead, the company has repeatedly sold new shares (multiple 424B5 offerings in 2026) to fix a Nasdaq stockholders' equity deficiency, which dilutes existing holders [5].

infrastructure.label: DEVELOPING
infrastructure.analysis: Scored mechanically as a Growth stock: 2.96 of 7 available weighted points (Forward P/E and PEG are unavailable and excluded), which rounds to 4. TTM revenue growth of 176% (1.00) is the only metric at target [6]. D/E of 138.9% (0.70), ROE of 9.0% (0.60, double weight), and a profit margin of just 1.0% (0.05) show a thin balance sheet, and H1 2026 gross margin fell to 16.5% from 24.0% [1][6]. The 5-year revenue CAGR is unavailable. A 3-year proxy is -13.9%, from $31.1M in 2022 to $19.9M in 2025, which scores 0.00 at double weight [6]. Liquidity of about $1.6M per day ($0.93 × 1.72M shares) barely clears the $1M floor, and recent sessions have traded far below average volume.

ai_resilience.label: MODERATE
ai_resilience.analysis: AI Risk Protection (7/9): Turbo sells physical inverters, batteries, and installed industrial storage. AI cannot replace energy storage hardware, and power demand from AI data centers is a tailwind for grid storage in general [2][3]. The real threat to the business is low-cost Chinese hardware competition, not AI substitution, so the AI risk score stays high but below immune because margins are thin and the products are commoditizing. AI Opportunity (0/1): The products are marketed as AI-optimized, but Turbo does not report AI-attributable revenue or software subscription revenue separately [4].

infinite_game.summary: Seen through Sinek's lens, Turbo Energy is a small company playing for survival rather than a cause. Its strategy in 2026 has been shaped by Nasdaq equity compliance deadlines, dilutive share sales, and one large industrial project, not by a lasting purpose. The move from residential to industrial storage shows some adaptability, but leadership's horizon is measured in listing-compliance cycles.

just_cause.analysis: Just Cause (1/3): 'Intelligent, accessible solar storage' points toward the energy transition, but it reads as product marketing and does not visibly guide decisions beyond chasing revenue [3][4].

courage_to_lead.analysis: Courage to Lead (0/2): Capital decisions in 2026 have been reactive. Leadership raised dilutive equity to clear a Nasdaq minimum stockholders' equity notice (January 2026 notice, regained compliance June 4) instead of making costly long-term bets [5].

trusting_teams.analysis: Trusting Teams (0/2): The CEO role changed hands within months of the 2023 IPO, and the company is governed by its controlling parent, Umbrella Solar Investment. We found no evidence of empowerment, retention, or a distinctive culture [3].

existential_flexibility.analysis: Existential Flexibility (1/2): Turbo expanded from residential all-in-one units into industrial and utility-scale storage, and that shift now drives most of its revenue. It has also entered the U.S. market [1][4]. These are meaningful adaptations but not a reinvention.

worthy_rivals.analysis: Worthy Rivals (0/1): Company communications focus on growth and listing milestones and do not frame competitors as rivals to learn from. We found no evidence of an infinite competitive mindset.

investment_thesis: Turbo Energy is a micro-cap (about $12M market cap) leveraged to European and U.S. demand for behind-the-meter and industrial storage. H1 2026 revenue rose about 173% to €15.0M, operating income turned positive (a €1.7M improvement), and the net loss narrowed to €65,647 from €1.4M [1]. If the 366 MWh industrial project leads to repeat utility-scale orders, this small revenue base could grow quickly, and the stock trades at about 0.5x TTM sales [2][6].
thesis_continued: The risks are severe. Growth depends on one large project, gross margin fell to 16.5% from 24.0%, and revenue has swung widely ($31.1M in 2022, $9.4M in 2024) [1][6]. The company received a Nasdaq minimum stockholders' equity deficiency notice in January 2026 and cured it only through dilutive offerings, and Nasdaq warned that a failure at the next periodic report could still lead to delisting [5]. With a share price below $1, it also faces minimum bid price risk, and daily dollar volume barely clears IOWN's $1M liquidity floor.
key_catalysts: Follow-on utility or industrial storage awards after delivery of the 366 MWh project, which would show H1 2026 growth is repeatable
U.S. distribution expansion of SUNBOX residential and SUNBOX Industry products
Full-year 2026 results showing sustained positive operating income and stockholders' equity above Nasdaq's $2.5M minimum
key_risks: Nasdaq listing risk: the stockholders' equity deficiency was cured only in June 2026, Nasdaq warned of delisting if compliance lapses at the next periodic report, and a sub-$1 share price adds minimum bid price exposure
Customer and project concentration: H1 2026 growth came mostly from one 366 MWh industrial project, and gross margin fell 750 bps to 16.5%
Dilution and commoditization: repeated 424B5 equity offerings plus price competition from much larger Chinese battery and inverter makers
